explain.say: The fungus changes the grass too. Where it releases nutrients the grass grows extra green, and where its threads are thick the soil can repel water and the grass turns brown. Each year the ring grows wider.

faq.q: Why do mushrooms grow in a ring?
faq.a: The fungus spreads outward from its starting point, and the threads in the middle die off once the food is used up. Only the healthy outer edge makes mushrooms, so they come up in a circle.

faq.q: Why does a fairy ring grow bigger?
faq.a: The living edge keeps moving outward into fresh soil with new food, so the ring widens, typically by several centimetres each year.

faq.q: Why is the grass different in a fairy ring?
faq.a: As the fungus breaks down dead material it releases nitrogen, which makes grass greener and lusher. Where its threads are dense, the soil can become water-repellent, so grass there may turn brown.
asks: Why is there a dark green circle on my lawn?

faq.q: How old can fairy rings be?
faq.a: Big rings can be very old. Some fairy rings are over 100 metres across and are thought to have been growing for hundreds of years.
asks: What is the biggest fairy ring?

faq.a: They are natural and mostly harmless, though they can spoil the look of a lawn. Some fairy ring mushrooms are poisonous, so never eat them without expert advice.
asks: Should I get rid of a fairy ring?

facts: A fairy ring forms because fungus threads spread outward from a central point and die off in the middle.
Some fairy rings are over 100 metres across and may be hundreds of years old.
The fairy ring champignon, Marasmius oreades, is one of the most common ring-forming fungi on lawns.
